newsitem.title: USA: U.S. study supports warmth for surgery patients.
newsitem.headline: U.S. study supports warmth for surgery patients.

text.p: Patients who have their body temperature kept at normal levels during and immediately after surgery run a 55 percent lower risk of suffering heart attacks, a study said Tuesday.

"These findings suggest that a certain proportion of early postoperative cardiac complications can be prevented by maintaining normothermia (normal temperature)," according to the report from the Johns Hopkins Medical Institutions in Baltimore.

Heart attacks are the leading cause of death during and immediately after surgery, the report said. The finding was based on a study of patients given supplemental warming by the use of a full-body warm air cover.
The researchers said heat may have a protective effect because it prevents the higher blood pressure and constriction of blood vessels that occur with hypothermia.
The study was published in this week's Journal of the American Medical Association.
